title: Fractional toggle notebook — preflight + quick triggers
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes for fractional toggles (0.1%–5%) when flipping model variants or routing policies. Meant to be a lightweight preflight checklist + one-liners I can paste during nights/weekends. NOT an official runbook — refine into playbook after next successful flip.

Context/assumptions:
- Target: reduce blast radius for new model/quantization profile flips.
- Platform: Hosted API + Dedicated fallback. Will use per-route traffic-sculpting + token-level sampling.
- Primary metrics: p50/p95 latency, early-failure-rate (5m rolling), server-error-rate (5xx), model-quality-regressions (BLEU/ROUGE proxies for eval requests), cost-per-token delta.

Preflight checks (quick):
- [ ] Confirm model artifact pinned in catalog (model@2025-02-15-quantB). If not pinned, create pin PR and wait 20m for artifact propagation.
- [ ] Ensure fallback route exists (route: /v1/gen -> model: model-stable) and traffic split can roll back to 100%.
- [ ] Verify warm caches: hit prefix cache with 50 synthetic requests across each region (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler headroom: reserved nodes >= expected concurrency*1.5. See /infra/autoscale/dashboard.
- [ ] Charting: open pinned dashboard (p50/p95, 5xx, client-latency, memory-evictions).
- [ ] Pagerduty rotation on-call notified (PD: infra-team, slack #canaryops).

Quick rolling steps (0.1% -> 5% ramp):
- Step 1 (0.1%): route expression 'rand() < 0.001 AND tenant in pilot-list' ; run 15m.
- Step 2 (0.5%): rand() < 0.005 ; 30m.
- Step 3 (1%): 45m.
- Step 4 (2.5%): 60m.
- Step 5 (5%): 90m.
- If any threshold breach: immediate -> rollback to previous stable percent and hold for 30m; escalate if persistent.

Thresholds (first-pass):
- p95 latency increase > 30% over baseline -> rollback.
- 5xx rate > 0.3% absolute -> rollback.
- Early-failure-rate (first token error) > 0.2% -> rollback and collect logs.
- ML quality sentinel: if eval-run on sampled responses shows > 3% regression on signal set -> pause and consult product (Maya).

Commands/snippets (copy-paste):
- Warm caches: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/warm -d '{"model":"model@2025-02-15-quantB","prefixes": ["/start","/chat"]}' # synthetic hits
- Set route split (k=v): curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood.api/routes/rl-123 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"traffic":{"model-stable":0.995,"model-canary":0.005}}'
- Quick check query (telemetry): GET https://ops-queries.redwood/api/query?expr=error_rate%5B5m%5D&route=rl-123

Observability notes (what to watch):
- Token-level burn: watch cost-per-token because quantB can spike GPU compute on long contexts (esp >512).
- KV-cache evictions: if eviction rate climbs, we might see p95 regressions; consider temporary cache-size bump.
- Tail latencies correlated with concurrency spikes -> may require autoscaler manual scale-up.

Riskiest failure modes (quick list):
- Silent degradation: model returns plausible but incorrect answers — need eval-set run and sample review.
- Resource exhaustion: unexpected memory growth from quant path -> OOM -> 5xx spike.
- Routing bug: mis-specified expression sends >50% traffic accidentally (test expressions in dry-run).

Rollback checklist (immediate):
- [ ] Set route back to 100% model-stable (paste route patch).
- [ ] Post brief note in #canaryops with timestamps, sample request ids, observed metric deltas.
- [ ] Create incident stub in status page if >10% of pilot cohort affected.
- [ ] Collect core dumps/log bundles: /infra/logpull --range=now-30m --route=rl-123

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add small synthetic eval harness that runs every ramp step automatically (canary-eval job).
- Wire up a model-quality webhook to slack #canaryops (so product sees regressions immediately).
- Verify quantization job reproducibility on dev machine (local run command saved in /home/asha/quant-check.sh).
- Short experiment: try 0.2% initial step next time to reduce variance in first window.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we require client opt-in for first 0.1% (tenant allowlist) or use pure random sampling? pros/cons — ask Jordan.
- Do we need a tighter p95 SL ack from Dedicated vs Hosted? Dedicated region us-west1 historically has 10% higher p95.

Historical notes (small):
- 2024-11: bumped from 1% to 5% and saw transient p95 spike for 20m; root cause was cache-priming race. Fixed by adding 60s priming wait.
- 2025-01: model flip with quantA succeeded; cost dropped ~8% at 5% traffic, no quality regressions on eval set.

If I get interrupted: minimal safe action = set traffic back to 100% stable + a Slack ping: "rolling back fractional flip due to spike — details in incident thread"

End of notes.

(Will move to shared drive playbook after one clean flip.)
